ingredients.item: Pork sausages (long, thin, such as chipolatas)

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Put the sausages on a rimmed baking sheet and roast 20 to 25 minutes, turning and shaking them once or twice, until browned. That should be about 160°F in the middle; a thermometer is optional. Without one, cut one open to check that it is no longer pink inside.

While the sausages roast, whisk the buckwheat flour, eggs, 1 tbsp of the oil and the salt in a large bowl until it looks like a thick paste. Slowly whisk in the milk until the batter is smooth. If you'd like, make the batter earlier in the day and keep it covered in the fridge.

Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and wipe it with a thin film of oil, tilting the pan to coat it. Pour in a ladleful of batter, about 1/3 cup, and swirl it to spread thin. Cook about 2 minutes, until the underside is browned and the edge lifts easily. Flip and cook 1 minute.
Slide the galette onto a plate and cover it to keep warm. Repeat with the rest of the batter, oiling the pan lightly between galettes, to make 8.
Let the sausages cool for a few minutes, then wrap each one in a galette. Serve warm, wrapped in a napkin to eat by hand.
method_notes: The only named galette saucisse recipe that could be read in full was Great British Chefs (Food Urchin), which has no ratings, so this is a fallback lead. Its batter is buckwheat flour, egg and milk, with sausages roasted while the galettes are fried. Sandwich Tribunal confirms the folded galette around a plain pork sausage but gives no amounts; it notes some cooks use an 80/20 buckwheat and wheat mix, and that mustard or onion jam are optional extras left out here. Made with 100% buckwheat as in the lead.
